title: Use analyzers and the portal · Level 1
slo: Choose and test an analyzer for a common extraction task.

exercises.question_text: What does a confidence score show for an extracted field value?

options.rationale: A confidence score indicates service certainty in an extracted value. It expresses confidence for that result.
An analyzer ID identifies the analyzer used. It does not measure certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when identifying the producing analyzer.

options.text: How text is arranged on a page
options.rationale: Text layout describes page arrangement. Confidence measures value certainty.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing document layout.

options.rationale: A schema defines fields before analysis. Confidence is returned for extracted values.
options.better_fit: Use this when describing extraction requirements.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Confidence measures service certainty in an extracted value.

exercises.question_text: What can a document image result in the portal include? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A document image result can include recognized text. This makes page content available for review.
A result can include layout information. Layout describes page text arrangement.
Fields can be mapped to extracted values. This connects a field name with its value.
Audio transcripts concern analyzed audio. Document images can return text, layout, and mapped fields.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing audio-analysis output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Document output can show text, layout, and mapped values.

exercises.question_text: A confidence score tells how text is arranged on a page.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A certainty measure would be used for the wrong purpose.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Confidence applies to values, while layout applies to page text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Layout describes arrangement; confidence describes certainty.

exercises.question_text: Where can you test an analyzer with uploaded material before coding?

options.rationale: The Foundry portal supports testing uploads and examples. It can be used before automation in code.
JSON is reviewed after analysis. It is not where testing begins.
options.better_fit: Use this to name structured output after analysis.

options.rationale: The API supports programmatic requests. The portal is the visual testing interface.
options.better_fit: Use this when automating analysis in an application.

options.rationale: An SDK client is used in application code. It is not the upload-and-test portal.
options.better_fit: Use this when implementing analysis in Python.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The portal supports testing before coding.

exercises.question_text: The portal can map a field such as Vendor address to its extracted value.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The link between a field and its value could be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Document analysis can map fields such as Vendor address to extracted values.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A result can show a field and its mapped value.

exercises.question_text: The Foundry portal can test an analyzer only after the workflow is automated in code.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An application could be built without checking returned fields.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the portal to test uploads before automating extraction.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Portal testing occurs before code automation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The field and its value would not be connected clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the portal action first, then the field and mapped value.

exercises.correct_answer: The portal maps Vendor address to 123 456th Street as its value
exercises.explanation: The portal can display a field such as Vendor address mapped to its extracted value.

exercises.question_text: Before automating extraction in code, you can test an analyzer in the new Foundry ___.

parts.text: Before automating extraction in code, you can test an analyzer in the new Foundry

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A result or coding tool would be named instead of the testing interface.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Choose portal for visual analyzer testing before coding.

exercises.explanation: The Foundry portal is used to test analyzers before code automation.

exercises.question_text: Which are listed prebuilt analyzer IDs? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: prebuilt-invoice is a supplied analyzer ID. It fits invoice analysis.
prebuilt-imageSearch is a listed prebuilt ID. It is supplied for a common scenario.
prebuilt-audioSearch is a listed prebuilt ID. It supports audio analysis.
custom-invoice is not a listed prebuilt ID. Custom analyzers are tailored by users.
options.better_fit: This could be a user-created analyzer name.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These are supplied IDs for common scenarios.

options.text: Analyzes input and returns structured results
options.rationale: An analyzer accepts content and applies AI analysis. It returns structured results.

options.text: Defines only the fields to extract
options.rationale: A schema defines fields and structure. An analyzer performs the analysis.
options.better_fit: This describes a schema used to define requested fields.

options.rationale: Storage happens after analysis returns results. It is not the analyzer's role.
options.better_fit: This fits a downstream system that saves returned JSON.

options.rationale: Data types may appear in a result. An analyzer does more than report metadata.
options.better_fit: This fits a description of typed result fields.

exercises.explanation: Correct. An analyzers accepts content, applies analysis, and returns structured output.

exercises.question_text: A custom analyzer is supplied for a common scenario without tailoring it to your requirements.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Custom analyzers are tailored to requirements and schema.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That describes a prebuilt analyzer.

exercises.question_text: A configured analyzer can reuse the same schema for every analysis request.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Similar inputs could produce inconsistent field structures.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A configured analyzer consistently reuses its extraction logic and schema.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Schema reuse makes repeated results predictable.

flashcards.back: A unit that analyzes input and returns structured results.
When extraction requirements and schema need tailoring.
To validate analyzer fields before automating in code.
How confident the service is in an extracted field value.
